translations.literal: Biographies 3: Sons and descendants of the Founding Ancestor — Wo Lu, Bei Lu, Xie Kude's grandson Bada, Xie Yibao's son Penna, Xie Lihu, Wu Guchu, Ba Hei, Chong Cheng (original name Puhui), He Sun's son Pu Jianu, Ma Po's son Man Douben, younger brother Man Douhe, son Man Du

translations.idiomatic: (Man Du's grandson Weirong, whose original name was Melie)

sentences.zh: 7.3.1 蠻睹孫 惟鎔

translations.literal: 7.3.1 Man Du's Grandson Weirong
translations.idiomatic: 7.3.1 Weirong, Grandson of Man Du

sentences.zh: 始祖明懿皇后生德帝烏魯，季曰斡魯，女曰注思版，皆福壽之語也。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor's Empress Mingyi bore Emperor De Wulu; the youngest son was called Wo Lu; a daughter was called Zhusi Ban — all names bearing words of blessing and longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor's Empress Mingyi gave birth to Emperor De Wulu; her youngest son was named Wo Lu, and a daughter Zhusi Ban — each name a word for fortune and long life.

sentences.zh: 以六十後生子，異之，故皆以嘉名名之焉。

translations.literal: Because she bore children after age sixty, it was considered extraordinary, and therefore they were all given auspicious names.
translations.idiomatic: Since she bore children only after turning sixty, the family regarded it as remarkable and gave each child an auspicious name.

sentences.zh: 德帝思皇后生安帝，季曰輩魯。

translations.literal: Emperor De's Empress Si bore Emperor An; the youngest son was Bei Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor De's Empress Si bore Emperor An and, as her youngest son, Bei Lu.

sentences.zh: 輩魯與獻祖俱徙海姑水，置屋宇焉。

translations.literal: Bei Lu and Xianzu together moved to the Haigu River and erected dwellings there.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Lu moved with Xianzu to the Haigu River, where they built houses.

sentences.zh: 輩魯之孫胡率。

translations.literal: Bei Lu's grandson Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Lu's line continued through his grandson Hulu.

sentences.zh: 胡率之子劾者，與景祖長子韓國公劾者同名。

translations.literal: Hulu's son Hezhe bore the same name as Jingzu's eldest son, Duke of Korea Hezhe.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu's son was named Hezhe — the same name as Jingzu's eldest son, the Duke of Korea.

sentences.zh: 韓國公前死，所謂肅宗納劾者之妻加古氏者是也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Korea had died earlier; this was the Gagu clan woman whom Suzong took as Hezhe's wife.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Korea had already died; this was the woman of the Gagu clan whom Suzong took as wife for the surviving Hezhe.

sentences.zh: 穆宗四年伐阿疏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Muzong, they campaigned against Ashu.
translations.idiomatic: In Muzong's fourth year, the clan marched against Ashu.

sentences.zh: 阿疏走遼。

translations.literal: Ashu fled to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Ashu fled into Liao territory.

sentences.zh: 遼使使來止伐阿疏軍。

translations.literal: Liao sent envoys to halt the army campaigning against Ashu.
translations.idiomatic: Liao dispatched envoys ordering a halt to the campaign against Ashu.

sentences.zh: 穆宗陽受遼帝約束，先歸國，留劾者守阿疏城。

translations.literal: Muzong outwardly accepted the Liao emperor's constraints, returned home first, and left Hezhe to hold Ashu's city.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong pretended to accept the Liao emperor's command, withdrew home first, and left Hezhe to hold Ashu's stronghold.

sentences.zh: 凡三年，卒攻破之。

translations.literal: After three years in all, they finally captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, they finally took the place by storm.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年贈特進。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, posthumously granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 15, he was posthumously granted the rank of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 謝庫德孫拔達 謝夷保子盆納 謝里忽

translations.literal: Xie Kude's grandson Bada; Xie Yibao's son Penna; Xie Lihu
translations.idiomatic: Bada, grandson of Xie Kude; Penna, son of Xie Yibao; and Xie Lihu

sentences.zh: 安帝節皇后生獻祖，次曰信德，次曰謝庫德，次曰謝夷保，次曰謝里忽。

translations.literal: Emperor An's Empress Jie bore Xianzu; next Xinde; next Xie Kude; next Xie Yibao; next Xie Lihu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An's Empress Jie bore Xianzu, then Xinde, Xie Kude, Xie Yibao, and Xie Lihu in succession.

sentences.zh: 謝庫德之孫拔達，謝夷保之子盆納，皆佐世祖有功。

translations.literal: Xie Kude's grandson Bada and Xie Yibao's son Penna both assisted Shizu with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Bada, grandson of Xie Kude, and Penna, son of Xie Yibao, both served Shizu with distinguished merit.

sentences.zh: 盆納勇毅善射，當時有與同名者，嘗有貳志，目之曰「惡盆納」。

translations.literal: Penna was brave, resolute, and skilled at archery; at the time there was another of the same name who once harbored divided loyalties, and they called him "Evil Penna."
translations.idiomatic: Penna was bold, steadfast, and a fine archer. Another man of the same name had once wavered in loyalty, so people distinguished them as "Evil Penna."

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，拔達贈儀同三司，盆納贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, Bada was posthumously granted Commissioner with Equal Protocol, and Penna Grand Commissioner with Equal Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 15, Bada was posthumously made Commissioner with Equal Protocol and Penna Grand Commissioner with Equal Protocol.

sentences.zh: 在世祖時，歡都、冶訶及劾者、拔達、盆納五人者，不離左右，親若手足，元勳之最著者也。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time, Huandu, Yehe, and Hezhe, Bada, and Penna — these five men never left his side; close as brothers; the most eminent of founding merit.
translations.idiomatic: During Shizu's rise, Huandu, Yehe, Hezhe, Bada, and Penna never left his side — close as brothers and the foremost of the founding meritocrats.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年皆配饗世祖廟廷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang, all were granted co-sacrifice in Shizu's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang year 5, all five were granted secondary sacrifice in Shizu's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 准德、束里保者，皆加古部人。

translations.literal: Zhuande and Shulibao were both of the Gagu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuande and Shulibao were both men of the Gagu clan.

sentences.zh: 申乃因、醜阿皆馳滿部人。

translations.literal: Shennaiyin and Chou'a were both of the Chiman clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shennaiyin and Chou'a were both of the Chiman clan.

sentences.zh: 富者粘沒罕，完顏部人。

translations.literal: Fuzhe Nianmohan was of the Wanyan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhe Nianmohan was a man of the Wanyan clan.

sentences.zh: 阿庫德、白達皆雅達瀾水完顏部勃董。

translations.literal: Akude and Baida were both tribal chiefs of the Yadalan River Wanyan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Akude and Baida were both chiefs of the Yadalan River branch of the Wanyan clan.

sentences.zh: 此七人者，當攜離之際，能一心竭力輔戴者也。

translations.literal: These seven men, at a time of dispersal, were able with one heart to exert themselves in support.
translations.idiomatic: These seven, when the clan was scattered and imperiled, stood firm and gave Shizu their wholehearted support.

sentences.zh: 達紀、胡蘇皆術甲部勃董。

translations.literal: Daji and Husu were both tribal chiefs of the Shujia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Daji and Husu were both chiefs of the Shujia clan.

sentences.zh: 勝昆、主保皆術虎部人。

translations.literal: Shengkun and Zhubao were both of the Shuhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shengkun and Zhubao were both men of the Shuhu clan.

sentences.zh: 阿庫德，溫蒂痕部人。

translations.literal: Akude was of the Wendihan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Akude was a man of the Wendihan clan.

sentences.zh: 此五人者，又其次者也。

translations.literal: These five men were the next rank below.
translations.idiomatic: These five ranked next among Shizu's supporters.

sentences.zh: 世祖初年，跋黑為變，烏春盛強，使人召阿庫德、白達。

translations.literal: In the early years of Shizu, Ba Hei rebelled; Wuchun was powerful and sent men to summon Akude and Baida.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizu's reign, Ba Hei rose in rebellion while Wuchun grew powerful and sent envoys to summon Akude and Baida.

sentences.zh: 阿庫德曰：「吾不知其他，死生與太師共之。」

translations.literal: Akude said: "I know nothing else — life and death I share with the Grand Preceptor."
translations.idiomatic: Akude said, "I know no other loyalty — life and death, I stand with the Grand Preceptor."

sentences.zh: 太師，謂世祖也。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor" meant Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor meant Shizu.

sentences.zh: 白達大喜曰：「我心正如此耳。

translations.literal: Baida rejoiced greatly and said: "My heart is exactly so.
translations.idiomatic: Baida was overjoyed. "That is exactly what is in my heart," he said.

sentences.zh: 烏春兵來，堅壁自守，勿與戰可也。」

translations.literal: When Wuchun's troops come, hold the walls and do not give battle — that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchun's army comes, hold your walls and do not engage — that will be enough.

sentences.zh: 達紀、胡蘇居琵里郭水，烏春兵出其間，不為變，終拒而不從。

translations.literal: Daji and Husu dwelt on the Piliguo River; Wuchun's army passed between them, yet they did not rebel and in the end refused to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Daji and Husu lived on the Piliguo River. Wuchun's forces marched between them, yet they never wavered and in the end refused to join him.

sentences.zh: 勝昆居胡不幹村，其兄滓不乃勃堇，烏春止其家，而以兵圍勝昆。

translations.literal: Shengkun dwelt at Hubugan village; his elder brother Zibunai was tribal chief; Wuchun lodged at his house while encircling Shengkun with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shengkun lived at Hubugan village. His elder brother Zibunai was a tribal chief; Wuchun stayed in Zibunai's house while surrounding Shengkun with troops.

sentences.zh: 烏春解去，世祖殺滓不乃，勝昆請無孥戮，世祖從之。

translations.literal: When Wuchun withdrew, Shizu killed Zibunai; Shengkun asked that his family not be punished to the last man, and Shizu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchun withdrew, Shizu executed Zibunai. Shengkun pleaded that the man's household not be wiped out, and Shizu granted it.

sentences.zh: 世祖破桓赧、散達，主保死焉。

translations.literal: When Shizu defeated Huanhan and Sandá, Zhubao died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu defeated Huanhan and Sandá, Zhubao fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，准德、申乃因、阿庫德、白達皆贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, Zhuande, Shennaiyin, Akude, and Baida were all posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 15, Zhuande, Shennaiyin, Akude, and Baida were all posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 束里保、醜阿、富者粘沒罕、達紀、胡蘇、勝昆、主保、溫蒂痕、阿庫德皆贈銀青光祿大夫，皆天會十五年追贈。

translations.literal: Shulibao, Chou'a, Fuzhe Nianmohan, Daji, Husu, Shengkun, Zhubao, Wendihan Akude were all posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal — all posthumously granted in the fifteenth year of Tianhui.
translations.idiomatic: Shulibao, Chou'a, Fuzhe Nianmohan, Daji, Husu, Shengkun, Zhubao, and the Wendihan Akude were all posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal — honors conferred together in Tianhui year 15.

sentences.zh: 又有胡論加古部勝昆勃堇、蟬春水烏延部富者郭赧，畏烏春強，請世祖兵出其間，以為重也。

translations.literal: There were also Huluen Gagu clan chief Shengkun and Chanqingshui Wuyan clan Fuzhe Guonán, who feared Wuchun's strength and asked that Shizu's army pass through their lands to lend weight.
translations.idiomatic: Two others feared Wuchun's power: Shengkun, chief of the Huluen Gagu clan, and Guonán of the Chanqingshui Wuyan clan. Each asked Shizu to march his forces through their territory so as to lend him greater weight.

sentences.zh: 世祖使斜列、躍盤將別軍過之。

translations.literal: Shizu sent Xielie and Yuepan to lead a separate army through.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu sent Xielie and Yuepan at the head of a detached force to pass through their lands.

sentences.zh: 郭赧教科列取先在烏春軍中二十二人，烏春覺之，殺二人，得二十人。

translations.literal: Guonán instructed Kelie to seize twenty-two men who had earlier been in Wuchun's army; Wuchun detected it, killed two, and twenty were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Guonán had Kelie seize twenty-two men who had once served in Wuchun's ranks. Wuchun caught wind of it and killed two, but twenty were still taken.

sentences.zh: 郭赧又以士人益斜列軍。

translations.literal: Guonán also added warriors to reinforce Xielie's army.
translations.idiomatic: Guonán also sent warriors to reinforce Xielie's force.

sentences.zh: 穆宗他日嘉此功不能忘，以斜列之女守甯妻郭赧子胡里罕焉。

translations.literal: Muzong later, cherishing this merit and unable to forget it, gave Xielie's daughter Shouning in marriage to Guonán's son Hulihan.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong never forgot this service and later gave Xielie's daughter Shouning in marriage to Guonán's son Hulihan.

sentences.zh: 婆多吐水裴滿部斡不勃堇附于世祖，桓赧焚之。

translations.literal: Botuoshui Piman clan chief Wobu attached himself to Shizu; Huanhan burned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wobu, chief of the Botuoshui Piman clan, had sided with Shizu, and Huanhan burned him alive.

sentences.zh: 斡不卒，世祖厚撫其家。

translations.literal: When Wobu died, Shizu treated his household generously.
translations.idiomatic: After Wobu's death, Shizu treated his household with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 因並錄之，以見立國之艱難雲。

translations.literal: They are therefore recorded together, to show how difficult the founding of the state was.
translations.idiomatic: They are recorded here together to show how arduous the founding of the state truly was.

sentences.zh: 謝里忽者，昭祖將定法制，諸父、國人不悅，已執昭祖，將殺之。

translations.literal: Xie Lihu: when Zhaozu was about to establish laws and institutions, the paternal uncles and clansmen were displeased; they had already seized Zhaozu and were about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: As for Xie Lihu: when Zhaozu set out to establish laws and institutions, his paternal uncles and the clansmen were displeased. They had already seized Zhaozu and were about to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 謝里忽亟往，彎弓注矢，射於眾中，眾乃散去，昭祖得免。

translations.literal: Xie Lihu hastened there, bent his bow and nocked an arrow, and shot into the crowd; the crowd then dispersed, and Zhaozu was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lihu rushed in, strung his bow, and loosed an arrow into the crowd. The assembly scattered, and Zhaozu was spared.

sentences.zh: 國俗，有被殺者，心使巫覡以詛祝殺之者，乃系刃於杖端，與眾至其家，歌而詛之曰：「取爾一角指天、一角指地之牛，無名之馬，向之則華面，背之則白尾，橫視之則有左右翼者。」

translations.literal: By national custom, when someone was killed, the bereaved would send a shaman to curse the killer; they tied blades to the ends of staves, went with a crowd to his house, and sang curses saying: "We take your ox with one horn pointing to heaven and one to earth, your nameless horse that shows a flowered face when approached and a white tail when turned away, that shows left and right wings when viewed sideways."
translations.idiomatic: By clan custom, when a man was slain, the bereaved family sent a shaman to curse the killer. Blades were tied to the ends of staves, and a crowd marched on his house singing: "We take your ox with one horn to heaven and one to earth, your nameless horse — flowered in the face when met, white in the tail when turned away, winged on either side when looked at askance."

sentences.zh: 其聲哀切淒婉，若《蒿里》之音。

translations.literal: The sound was mournful, piercing, and plaintive, like the tune of "Haoli."
translations.idiomatic: Their voices were mournful and piercing, like the dirge of "Haoli."

sentences.zh: 既而以刃畫地，劫取畜產財物而還。

translations.literal: Then with blades they marked the ground and seized livestock and goods before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Then they scored the ground with their blades and carried off livestock and goods before departing.

sentences.zh: 其家一經詛祝，家道輒敗。

translations.literal: Once a household had been cursed in this way, its fortunes at once collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Once a household fell under such a curse, its fortunes collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 及來流水烏薩紮部殺完顏部人，昭祖往烏薩紮部以國俗治之，大有所獲，頒之于諸父昆弟而不及謝里忽。

translations.literal: When the Laishui Wusazha clan killed men of the Wanyan clan, Zhaozu went to the Wusazha clan and dealt with them by national custom, gaining much; he distributed the spoils among his paternal uncles and brothers but not to Xie Lihu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Laishui Wusazha clan killed Wanyan clansmen, Zhaozu went to Wusazha and settled the matter by clan law, taking a rich settlement. He divided the spoils among his paternal uncles and brothers but gave nothing to Xie Lihu.

sentences.zh: 謝里忽曰：「前日免汝于死者吾之力，往治烏薩紮部者吾之謀也。

translations.literal: Xie Lihu said: "The other day it was my strength that spared you from death; the plan to go deal with the Wusazha clan was mine.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lihu said, "It was I who saved you from death the other day, and it was my counsel that sent you against the Wusazha clan.

sentences.zh: 分不及我。

translations.literal: Yet in the division I was not included.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I received no share of the spoils.

sentences.zh: 何邪。」

translations.literal: Why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?"

sentences.zh: 昭祖於是早起，自齎間金列鞢往饋之。

translations.literal: Zhaozu thereupon rose early, himself carrying a gold-inlaid belt plaque to present to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu rose early the next morning and went himself, bearing a gold-inlaid belt plaque as a gift.

sentences.zh: 時謝里忽猶未起，擁寢衣而問曰：「爾為誰？」

translations.literal: At the time Xie Lihu had not yet risen; clutching his sleeping robe he asked: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lihu had not yet risen. Clutching his sleeping robe, he asked, "Who is there?"

sentences.zh: 昭祖曰：「石魯先擇此寶，而後頒及他人，敢私布之。」

translations.literal: Zhaozu said: "Shilu chose this treasure first, then distributed to others; I venture to offer it to you privately."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu said, "Shilu chose this treasure for you before sharing with the others — I bring it to you privately."

sentences.zh: 謝里忽既揚言，初不自安，至是乃大喜。

translations.literal: Xie Lihu, having spoken out publicly, had at first not felt secure; now he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lihu had spoken out in anger and felt uneasy afterward; now he was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 列鞢者，腰佩也。

translations.literal: Lie die means a waist pendant.
translations.idiomatic: A lie die was a belt pendant worn at the waist.

sentences.zh: 烏古出 跋黑

translations.literal: Wu Guchu; Ba Hei
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guchu and Ba Hei

sentences.zh: 獻祖恭靖皇后生昭祖，次曰樸都，次曰阿保寒，次曰敵酷，次曰敵古乃，次曰撒里輦，次曰撒葛周。

translations.literal: Xianzu's Empress Gongjing bore Zhaozu; next Pudu; next Abaohan; next Diku; next Digunai; next Salinian; next Sagezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu's Empress Gongjing bore Zhaozu, then in succession Pudu, Abaohan, Diku, Digunai, Salinian, and Sagezhou.

sentences.zh: 昭祖威順皇后生景祖，次曰烏古出。

translations.literal: Zhaozu's Empress Weishun bore Jingzu; next Wu Guchu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu's Empress Weishun bore Jingzu and, as her next son, Wu Guchu.

sentences.zh: 次室達胡末，烏薩紮部人，生跋黑、僕里黑、斡里安。

translations.literal: A secondary consort, Dahu'mo, of the Wusazha clan, bore Ba Hei, Pulihai, and Wolian.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary wife, Dahu'mo of the Wusazha clan, bore Ba Hei, Pulihai, and Wolian.

sentences.zh: 次室高麗人，生胡失答。

translations.literal: A secondary consort, a Koryo woman, bore Hushida.
translations.idiomatic: Another secondary wife, a woman of Koryo, bore Hushida.

sentences.zh: 烏古出，初昭祖久無子，有巫者能道神語，甚驗，乃往禱焉。

translations.literal: Wu Guchu: at first Zhaozu long had no sons; there was a shaman who could speak the language of spirits, very efficacious, and he went to pray.
translations.idiomatic: As for Wu Guchu: Zhaozu had long been without sons. There was a shaman famed for speaking with spirits, and Zhaozu went to pray through him.

sentences.zh: 巫良久曰：「男子之魂至矣。

translations.literal: After a long while the shaman said: "The soul of a male has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the shaman said, "A male soul has arrived.

sentences.zh: 此子厚有福德，子孫昌盛；

translations.literal: This child is richly endowed with fortune and virtue; descendants will flourish;
translations.idiomatic: This child is richly blessed; his line will flourish;

sentences.zh: 可拜而受之。

translations.literal: you may bow and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: bow and receive him.

sentences.zh: 若生，則名之曰烏古乃。」

translations.literal: If he is born, name him Wugunai."
translations.idiomatic: If he is born, name him Wugunai."

sentences.zh: 是為景祖。

translations.literal: This was Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: This was Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 又良久曰：「女子之魂至矣，可名曰五鵶忍。」

translations.literal: After another long while he said: "The soul of a female has arrived; she may be named Wuyaren."
translations.idiomatic: After another long pause he said, "A female soul has come — name her Wuyaren."

sentences.zh: 又良久曰：「女子之兆複見，可名曰斡都拔。」

translations.literal: After another long while he said: "The omen of a female appears again; she may be named Wuduba."
translations.idiomatic: Again after a long silence: "Another female omen — name her Wuduba."

sentences.zh: 又久之，複曰：「男子之兆複見，然性不馴良，長則殘忍，無親親之恩，必行非義，不可受也。」

translations.literal: After still longer, he again said: "The omen of a male appears again, yet his nature is not docile; grown he will be cruel, without affection for kin, certain to commit wrong — he must not be received."
translations.idiomatic: After still longer silence he said again, "A male omen returns — but his nature will not be tame. Grown, he will be cruel, without love for kin, sure to do wrong. Do not receive him."

sentences.zh: 昭祖方念後嗣未立，乃曰：「雖不良，亦願受之。」

translations.literal: Zhaozu, just then anxious that no heir was established, said: "Though he is not good, I still wish to receive him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu, anxious that he still had no heir, said, "Even if he is ill-favored, I will receive him."

sentences.zh: 巫者曰：「當名之曰烏古出。」

translations.literal: The shaman said: "He should be named Wu Guchu."
translations.idiomatic: The shaman said, "Name him Wu Guchu."

sentences.zh: 既而生二男二女，其次弟先後皆如巫者之言，遂以巫所命名名之。

translations.literal: In time two sons and two daughters were born; the order of the younger brothers and sisters all matched the shaman's words, and they were therefore given the names the shaman had assigned.
translations.idiomatic: In time two sons and two daughters were born, each in the order the shaman had foretold, and each received the name he had given.

sentences.zh: 景祖初立，烏古出酗酒，屢悖威順皇后。

translations.literal: When Jingzu was first established, Wu Guchu drank heavily and repeatedly defied Empress Weishun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Jingzu took leadership, Wu Guchu drank heavily and repeatedly defied Empress Weishun.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「巫言驗矣，悖亂之人終不可留。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "The shaman's words have proved true; a rebellious man cannot in the end be kept."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "The shaman spoke true — a man so rebellious cannot be kept."

sentences.zh: 遂與景祖謀而殺之。

translations.literal: She then plotted with Jingzu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: She plotted with Jingzu and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 部人怒曰：「此子性如此，在國俗當主父母之業，奈何殺之？」

translations.literal: Clansmen were angry and said: "This son's nature is such — by national custom he should head the parents' household; how could you kill him?"
translations.idiomatic: The clansmen were furious. "By our custom such a son heads the parents' household — how could you kill him?"

sentences.zh: 欲殺景祖。

translations.literal: They wished to kill Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to kill Jingzu in revenge.

sentences.zh: 後乃匿景祖，出謂眾曰：「為子而悖其母，率是而行，將焉用之？

translations.literal: The empress then hid Jingzu and went out to address the crowd: "As a son who defies his mother — if he goes on in this way, of what use is he?
translations.idiomatic: The empress hid Jingzu and went out to face the crowd. "A son who defies his mother — if that is how he conducts himself, what good is he?

sentences.zh: 吾割愛而殺之，烏古乃不知也，汝輩寧殺我乎？」

translations.literal: I cut off my affection and killed him; Wugunai did not know — would you rather kill me?"
translations.idiomatic: I slew my own son, and Wugunai knew nothing of it. Will you kill me instead?"

sentences.zh: 眾乃罷去。

translations.literal: The crowd then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd dispersed.

sentences.zh: 烏古出之子習不失，自有傳。

translations.literal: Wu Guchu's son Xibushi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guchu's son Xibushi has his own biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 跋黑及同母弟二人，自幼時每爭攘飲食，昭祖見而惡之，曰：「吾娶此妾而生子如此，後必為子孫之患。」

translations.literal: Ba Hei and his two younger brothers of the same mother, from childhood constantly fought over food and drink; Zhaozu saw it and detested them, saying: "I took this concubine and bore sons like these — later they will surely be a trouble to descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Ba Hei and his two full brothers had fought over food and drink since childhood. Zhaozu saw it and said in disgust, "I took this concubine and bore sons like these — they will surely trouble our descendants."

sentences.zh: 世祖初立，跋黑果有異志，誘桓赧、散達、烏春、窩謀罕離間部屬，使貳于世祖。

translations.literal: When Shizu was first established, Ba Hei indeed harbored a different intent, enticing Huanhan, Sandá, Wuchun, and Womouhan to divide the clansmen and make them turn against Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu first rose, Ba Hei did harbor separate ambitions, drawing Huanhan, Sandá, Wuchun, and Womouhan to split the clansmen and turn them against Shizu.

sentences.zh: 世祖患之，乃加意事之，使為勃堇而不令典兵。

translations.literal: Shizu was troubled by this and therefore treated him with special attention, making him tribal chief but not allowing him to command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was troubled by this and treated Ba Hei with deliberate favor — made him a tribal chief but gave him no command of troops.

sentences.zh: 跋黑既陰與桓赧、烏春謀計，國人皆知之，而童謠有「欲征則附于跋黑，欲死則附於劾里缽、頗刺淑」之語。

translations.literal: Ba Hei had secretly plotted with Huanhan and Wuchun; the clansmen all knew it, and children's songs had the words: "If you wish to campaign, attach to Ba Hei; if you wish to die, attach to Helibo and Pocishu."
translations.idiomatic: Ba Hei had been plotting in secret with Huanhan and Wuchun, and the whole clan knew it. A children's rhyme ran: "Want war — follow Ba Hei; want death — follow Helibo and Pocishu."

sentences.zh: 世祖亦以策探得兄弟部人向背。

translations.literal: Shizu also by stratagem probed where the brothers' clansmen stood.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu used the rhyme as a stratagem to learn which way his brothers' clansmen leaned.

sentences.zh: 烏春、桓赧相次以兵來攻，世祖外禦強兵，而內畏跋黑之變。

translations.literal: Wuchun and Huanhan in succession came with troops to attack; Shizu faced strong armies outwardly while inwardly fearing Ba Hei's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun and Huanhan attacked in turn. Shizu fought powerful enemies abroad while fearing Ba Hei's revolt at home.

sentences.zh: 將行，聞跋黑食於其愛妾之父家，肉張咽而死，且喜且悲，乃迎屍而哭之。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he heard that Ba Hei was dining at his favorite concubine's father's house and choked to death on swollen meat in his throat; both pleased and grieved, he went to meet the corpse and wept over it.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to march, word came that Ba Hei had been dining at his favorite concubine's father's house and choked to death on a piece of meat. Shizu was both relieved and grieved; he met the corpse and wept over it.

sentences.zh: 景祖昭肅皇后生韓國公劾者，次世祖，次沂國公劾孫，次肅宗，次穆宗。

translations.literal: Jingzu's Empress Zhaosu bore the Korea Duke Hezhe, next Shizu, next Yiguo Duke He Sun, next Suzong, next Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu's Empress Zhaosu bore the Korea Duke Hezhe, then Shizu, the Yiguo Duke He Sun, Suzong, and Muzong.

sentences.zh: 次室注思灰，契丹人，生代國公劾真保。

translations.literal: The secondary consort Zhusihui, a Khitan, bore Daiguo Duke He Zhenbao.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary consort, Zhusihui, a Khitan woman, bore the Daiguo Duke He Zhenbao.

sentences.zh: 次室溫迪痕氏，名敵本，生虞國公麻頗、隋國公阿離合懣、鄭國公謾都訶。

translations.literal: The secondary consort of the Wendihn clan, named Diben, bore Yuguo Duke Ma Po, Suiguo Duke Alihemen, and Zhengguo Duke Man Douhe.
translations.idiomatic: Another secondary consort of the Wendihn clan, Diben, bore the Yuguo Duke Ma Po, the Suiguo Duke Alihemen, and the Zhengguo Duke Man Douhe.

sentences.zh: 劾者、阿離合懣別有傳。

translations.literal: Hezhe and Alihemen have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhe and Alihemen are treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 劾孫。

translations.literal: He Sun.
translations.idiomatic: He Sun.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年大封宗室，劾孫追封王爵。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui, when the imperial clan was greatly enfeoffed, He Sun was posthumously enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 14, when the imperial clan received major enfeoffments, He Sun was posthumously raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 正隆例降封鄭國公。

translations.literal: Under the Zhenglong precedent, he was reduced to Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong precedents, his rank was reduced to Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 子 浦家奴

translations.literal: Son: Pu Jianu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Pu Jianu

sentences.zh: 子蒲家奴又名昱，嘗從太祖伐留可、塢塔。

translations.literal: The son Pu Jianu, also named Yu, once followed Taizu in campaigns against Liuke and Wuta.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pu Jianu, also called Yu, campaigned with Taizu against Liuke and Wuta.

sentences.zh: 太祖使蒲家奴招詐都，詐都即降。

translations.literal: Taizu sent Pu Jianu to summon Zhadu; Zhadu at once surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Pu Jianu to summon Zhadu, who surrendered immediately.

sentences.zh: 康宗八年，系遼籍女直紇石烈部阿里保太彎阻兵，招納亡命，邊民多亡歸之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangzong, Aribao Taiwan of the Liao-registered Nüzhi Heshilie clan raised troops in defiance, recruited fugitives, and many border people fled to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangzong year 8, Aribao Taiwan of the Liao-registered Nüzhi Heshilie clan rebelled, sheltering fugitives; many border people fled to his side.

sentences.zh: 蒲家奴以偏師夜行書止，抵石勒水，襲擊破之，盡俘其孥而還。

translations.literal: Pu Jianu with a detached force marched by night until dawn, reached the Shile River, struck and routed them, captured all their wives and children, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Jianu led a detached force by night until dawn, reached the Shile River, routed the rebels, took all their families captive, and returned.

sentences.zh: 邊氓自此無複亡者。

translations.literal: From then on no border people fled away again.
translations.idiomatic: After that, border people no longer fled to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 後與宗雄視泰州地土，太祖因徙萬家屯田於其地。

translations.literal: Later, together with Zongxiong he surveyed the land of Taizhou; Taizu therefore moved ten thousand households to farm colony there.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Zongxiong surveyed Taizhou's lands, and Taizu relocated ten thousand households to farm there.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年，蒲家奴為吳勃極烈，遂為都統，使襲遼帝，而以雨潦不果行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, Pu Jianu became Wubo Bolie, then supreme commander, and was sent to attack the Liao emperor, but rain and flooding prevented the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year 5, Pu Jianu became Wubo Bolie and then supreme commander; he was ordered to strike at the Liao emperor, but rains and floods prevented the march.

sentences.zh: 既而，忽魯勃極烈杲都統內外諸軍以取中京，蒲家奴等皆為之副。

translations.literal: Thereafter, Hulu Bolie Gao commanded the supreme command of inner and outer armies to take Zhongjing; Pu Jianu and others all served as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Hulu Bolie Gao took supreme command of all forces, inner and outer, to seize Zhongjing; Pu Jianu and others served as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 遼帝西走，都統杲使蒲家奴以兵一千助撻懶擊遼都統馬哥，與撻懶不相及，蒲家奴與賽里、斜野降其西北居延之眾。

translations.literal: The Liao emperor fled west; Commander Gao sent Pu Jianu with a thousand troops to assist Talan in striking Liao Commander Mage; not meeting Talan, Pu Jianu with Saili and Xieye subdued the northwestern masses at Juyan.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor fled west. Commander Gao sent Pu Jianu with a thousand men to help Talan strike the Liao commander Mage; failing to join Talan, Pu Jianu with Saili and Xieye brought the northwestern people of Juyan to surrender.

sentences.zh: 而降民稍複逃散，毗室部亦叛，遂率兵襲之。

translations.literal: But the surrendered people gradually fled and scattered again, and the Pishi clan also rebelled; he therefore led troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered people soon began fleeing again, and the Pishi clan rebelled as well; he marched against them.

sentences.zh: 至鐵呂川，遇敵八千，遂力戰，兵敗。

translations.literal: Reaching Tielüchuan, they encountered eight thousand enemies and fought hard, but the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Tielüchuan they met eight thousand enemy troops, fought hard, and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 察刺以兵來會，追及敵兵于黃水，獲畜產甚眾。

translations.literal: Chaci came with troops to join; pursuing the enemy at Huangshui, they captured a great quantity of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Chaci arrived with reinforcements; pursuing the enemy to Huangshui, they seized vast herds of livestock.

sentences.zh: 是役也，奧燉按打海被十一創，竟敗敵兵而還。

translations.literal: In this campaign, Aodan Andahai received eleven wounds yet still routed the enemy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle Aodan Andahai took eleven wounds yet still routed the enemy and returned.

sentences.zh: 軍于旺國崖西。

translations.literal: The army encamped west of Wangguoya.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped west of Wangguoya.

sentences.zh: 賽里亦以兵會太祖，自草濼追遼帝，蒲家奴、宗望為前鋒，戒之曰：「彼若深溝高壘，未可與戰，即偵伺巡邏，勿令遁去，以俟大軍。

translations.literal: Saili also came with troops to join Taizu; from Caopao they pursued the Liao emperor; Pu Jianu and Zongwang were vanguard; he warned them: "If they have deep moats and high ramparts, do not engage — only scout and patrol, do not let them escape, and await the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Saili also joined Taizu and, from Caopao, pursued the Liao emperor. Pu Jianu and Zongwang led the vanguard. Taizu warned them: "If the enemy has deep moats and high walls, do not give battle — scout and patrol, keep them from escaping, and wait for the main army.

sentences.zh: 若其無備，便可擊也。」

translations.literal: If they are unprepared, you may strike."
translations.idiomatic: If they are unprepared, strike at once."

sentences.zh: 上次胡離畛川，吳十、馬和尚至小魚濼，夜潛入遼主營，執新羅奴以還，送知遼帝所在。

translations.literal: Taizu reached Hulizhenchuan; Wu Shi and the Monk Ma reached Xiaoyupao; by night they secretly entered the Liao ruler's camp, seized Xinluonu and returned, reporting where the Liao ruler was.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu reached Hulizhenchuan. Wu Shi and Monk Ma reached Xiaoyupao and by night stole into the Liao ruler's camp, seized Xinluonu, and returned with word of the Liao ruler's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 蒲家奴等晝夜兼行，追及于石輦鐸。

translations.literal: Pu Jianu and others marched day and night without rest, caught up at Shinianduo.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Jianu and the others pressed on day and night and caught up at Shinianduo.

sentences.zh: 我兵四千，至者才千人，遼兵圍之。

translations.literal: Our army was four thousand, but only a thousand had arrived when Liao troops surrounded them.
translations.idiomatic: Their force numbered four thousand, but only a thousand had come up when Liao troops surrounded them.

sentences.zh: 余睹指遼帝麾蓋，騎兵馳之，遼帝遁去，兵遂潰，所殺甚眾。

translations.literal: Yudu pointed at the Liao emperor's banner and canopy; cavalry charged; the Liao emperor fled; the army collapsed; the slain were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu pointed at the Liao emperor's banner and canopy; the cavalry charged; the Liao emperor fled and his army collapsed; the dead were innumerable.

sentences.zh: 麻頗，天會十五年封王，正隆例封虞國公。

translations.literal: Ma Po, in the fifteenth year of Tianhui enfeoffed as prince; under the Zhenglong precedent enfeoffed as Yuguo Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Po was enfeoffed as a prince in Tianhui year 15; under the Zhenglong precedents he held the rank of Yuguo Duke.

sentences.zh: 子 謾都本

translations.literal: Son: Man Douben
translations.idiomatic: Son: Man Douben

sentences.zh: 長子謾都本，孝友恭謹，多謀而善戰。

translations.literal: The eldest son Man Douben was filial, friendly, reverent, and careful, resourceful and skilled in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Man Douben was filial, courteous, and careful — shrewd in counsel and formidable in battle.

sentences.zh: 年十五，隸軍中，從攻窩盧歡。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he entered the army and followed in the attack on Woluhuan.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he entered the ranks and joined the attack on Woluhuan.

sentences.zh: 及系遼女直胡失荅等為變，謾都本自為質，遂從胡失荅歸，中途以計殺守者而還。

translations.literal: When the Liao-registered Nüzhi Hushida and others rebelled, Man Douben offered himself as hostage, then followed Hushida home; midway he by stratagem killed the guards and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Hushida and other Liao-registered Nüzhi rebelled, Man Douben gave himself up as a hostage and went with Hushida; midway he tricked and killed the guards and made his escape.

sentences.zh: 攻甯江州，敢黃龍府，破高永昌，取春、泰州，皆有功，多受賞賚，遂為謀克。

translations.literal: In the attack on Ningjiangzhou, daring against Huanglongfu, breaking Gao Yongchang, taking Chun and Taizhou — all had merit; he received many rewards and was made mouke.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself at Ningjiangzhou, at Huanglongfu, against Gao Yongchang, and in the capture of Chun and Taizhou; richly rewarded, he was made a mouke.

sentences.zh: 討嶺東未服州郡。

translations.literal: He campaigned against the unsubdued prefectures east of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the unsubdued prefectures beyond the eastern passes.

sentences.zh: 過土河東山，敗賊三千人。

translations.literal: Crossing east of the Thu River, he defeated three thousand bandits.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Thu River he routed three thousand bandits.

sentences.zh: 奚、契丹寇土河西，與猛安蒙葛、麻吉擊之。

translations.literal: Xi and Khitan raided west of the Thu River; together with Meng'an Mengge and Maji he struck them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi and Khitan raiders struck west of the Thu River, he joined Meng'an Mengge and Maji in driving them off.

sentences.zh: 謾都本對敵之中，推鋒力戰，破其眾九萬人。

translations.literal: Man Douben amid the enemy pushed the vanguard and fought hard, breaking their force of ninety thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Man Douben led the charge in the thick of the enemy and broke a force of ninety thousand.

sentences.zh: 奚眾萬余保阿鄰甸，複擊敗之，降其旁近居人。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Xi held Alindian; he again struck and defeated them and reduced the nearby inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Xi held Alindian; he defeated them again and brought the neighboring peoples to submission.

sentences.zh: 複以五百騎破遼兵一千，生擒其將以歸。

translations.literal: Again with five hundred cavalry he broke a thousand Liao troops and captured their general alive and returned.
translations.idiomatic: With five hundred horsemen he routed a thousand Liao troops and returned with their general as a captive.

sentences.zh: 與闍母攻興中府，中流矢卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: With Chanmu he attacked Xingzhongfu; struck by a flying arrow he died, age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Xingzhongfu with Chanmu, he was struck by an arrow and died at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 天眷中，贈金紫光祿大夫，諡英毅。

translations.literal: In the Tianjuan era, posthumously granted Golden Purple Light Grand Master; posthumous title Yingyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjuan era he was posthumously granted Golden Purple Light Grand Master with the posthumous title Yingyi, "Resolute Valor."

sentences.zh: 弟 謾都訶

translations.literal: Younger brother: Man Douhe
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Man Douhe

sentences.zh: 謾都訶，屢從征伐，天會二年為阿舍勃極烈，參議國政，明年薨。

translations.literal: Man Douhe repeatedly followed on campaigns; in the second year of Tianhui became Asher Bolie, deliberating on state affairs; the next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Man Douhe campaigned repeatedly; in Tianhui year 2 he became Asher Bolie and joined in deliberating state affairs; he died the following year.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，大封宗室，追封王。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, when the imperial clan was greatly enfeoffed, he was posthumously enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 15, when the imperial clan received major enfeoffments, he was posthumously raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 正隆例封鄭國公，明昌五年，諡定濟。

translations.literal: Under the Zhenglong precedent enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng; in the fifth year of Mingchang, posthumous title Dingji.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong precedents he held the rank of Duke of Zheng; in Mingchang year 5 he received the posthumous title Dingji, "Steadfast Relief."

sentences.zh: 子 蠻睹

translations.literal: Son: Man Du
translations.idiomatic: Son: Man Du

sentences.zh: 蠻睹，襲父麻頗猛安。

translations.literal: Man Du succeeded his father Ma Po as meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Man Du inherited his father Ma Po's post as meng'an.

sentences.zh: 蠻睹卒，子掃合襲。

translations.literal: When Man Du died, his son Saoge succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Man Du died, his son Saoge succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 掃合卒，子撒合輦襲。

translations.literal: When Saoge died, his son Sahenian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Saoge died, his son Sahenian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 撒合輦卒，子惟鎔襲。

translations.literal: When Sahenian died, his son Weirong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Sahenian died, his son Weirong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 蠻睹孫 惟鎔

translations.literal: Man Du's grandson: Weirong
translations.idiomatic: Man Du's grandson: Weirong

sentences.zh: 惟鎔本名沒烈，字子鑄，駢脅多力，喜周急人。

translations.literal: Weirong's original name was Melie, courtesy name Zizhu; he had joined ribs and great strength, and delighted in relieving others' urgent needs.
translations.idiomatic: Weirong, originally named Melie and styled Zizhu, had fused ribs and immense strength and delighted in helping others in distress.

sentences.zh: 至甯初，守楊文關有功，兼都統，護漕運。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhi'ning era, he had merit defending Yangwen Pass, concurrently served as supreme commander, and guarded grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhi'ning era he distinguished himself defending Yangwen Pass, served concurrently as supreme commander, and guarded grain shipments.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，佩金牌護親軍家屬遷汴，遙授同知祁州軍州事，充提控。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, wearing a golden tablet he escorted the households of the imperial guard to Bian; remotely appointed Vice Commissioner of Qizhou Prefecture and Army Affairs, and served as tìkong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou year 2, bearing a golden tablet he escorted the imperial guard families to Bian; he was remotely appointed Vice Commissioner of Qizhou military and civil affairs and served as tìkong.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，破紅襖賊於大沫堌，惟鎔入自北門，諸軍繼進，生獲劉二祖，功最。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou, he broke the Red-Turban bandits at Damogu; Weirong entered from the north gate; the armies followed; Liu Erzu was captured alive; his merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou year 3 he routed the Red-Turban rebels at Damogu; Weirong entered by the north gate as the armies poured in behind him and took Liu Erzu alive — the foremost merit of the battle.

sentences.zh: 遷泰安軍節度副使，改遂王府尉幄都水少監、東平府治中。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Tai'an Army; changed to Palace Commandant of Suiting of the Suifuwei, Director of Waterworks Junior Supervisor, and Prefectural Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Tai'an Army, then made Palace Commandant of Suiting under the Suifuwei, Junior Director of Waterworks, and Administrator of Dongping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐誤以刃傷同知府事紇石烈牙吾塔，當削降殿年，仍從軍自效。

translations.literal: Because he accidentally wounded with a blade the Co-Prefect Heshilie Yawuta, he should have been demoted and lost years of seniority; nevertheless he was sent to the army to redeem merit.
translations.idiomatic: He accidentally wounded Co-Prefect Heshilie Yawuta with a blade and should have been demoted and stripped of seniority; instead he was sent back to the ranks to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 討花帽賊于曹、濟間，行省蒙古綱奏其功，複前職。

translations.literal: Campaigning against the Flower-Cap bandits between Cao and Ji, the Provincial Commissioner Mongke Gang memorialized his merit; his former offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against the Flower-Cap rebels between Cao and Ji, Provincial Commissioner Mongke Gang memorialized his merit and his former offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 遷邳州經略使，卒。

translations.literal: Promoted to Military Commissioner of Pizhou; died.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Military Commissioner of Pizhou, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 子從傑襲猛安，累功遙授鎮南軍節度副使。

translations.literal: His son Congjie succeeded as meng'an; by accumulated merit he was remotely appointed Vice Military Commissioner of Zhennan Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congjie inherited the meng'an post; by accumulated merit he was remotely appointed Vice Military Commissioner of Zhennan Army.

sentences.zh: 世祖翼簡皇后生康宗，次太祖，次魏王斡帶，次太宗，次遼王斜也。

translations.literal: Shizu's Empress Yijian bore Kangzong, next Taizu, next Wei Prince Wo Dai, next Taizong, next Liao Prince Xieye.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu's Empress Yijian bore Kangzong, then Taizu, the Wei Prince Wo Dai, Taizong, and the Liao Prince Xieye.

sentences.zh: 次室徒單氏生衛王斡賽，次魯王斡者。

translations.literal: The secondary consort Tushi bore Wei Prince Wo Sai, next Lu Prince Wozhe.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary consort of the Tushi clan bore the Wei Prince Wo Sai and the Lu Prince Wozhe.

sentences.zh: 次室僕散氏生漢王烏故乃。

translations.literal: The secondary consort Pusan bore Han Prince Wugunai.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary consort of the Pusan clan bore the Han Prince Wugunai.

sentences.zh: 次室術虎氏生魯王闍母。

translations.literal: The secondary consort Shihu bore Lu Prince Chanmu.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary consort of the Shihu clan bore the Lu Prince Chanmu.

sentences.zh: 次室術虎氏生沂王查刺。

translations.literal: The secondary consort Shihu bore Yi Prince Zhachi.
translations.idiomatic: Another secondary consort of the Shihu clan bore the Yi Prince Zhachi.

sentences.zh: 次室烏古論氏生鄆王昂。

translations.literal: The secondary consort Wugulun bore Yun Prince Ang.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary consort of the Wugulun clan bore the Yun Prince Ang.

sentences.zh: 斡帶，年二十餘，撒改伐留可，斡帶與習不失、阿里合懣等俱為裨將。

translations.literal: Wo Dai, a little over twenty, Sagai attacked Liuke; Wo Dai with Xishibu, Alihemen, and others all served as deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo Dai was barely twenty, Sagai attacked Liuke; Wo Dai served with Xishibu, Alihemen, and others as deputy generals.

sentences.zh: 諸將議攻取，斡帶主攻城便。

translations.literal: The generals debated whether to attack; Wo Dai advocated that assaulting the city was the better course.
translations.idiomatic: The generals debated the assault; Wo Dai argued that a direct attack on the city was best.

sentences.zh: 太祖將至軍，斡帶迎之，謂太祖曰：「留可城且下，忽惑他議。」

translations.literal: Taizu was about to reach the army; Wo Dai went to meet him and said to Taizu: "Liuke's city is about to fall, but suddenly other plans arose."
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu was marching to join the army, Wo Dai met him and said, "Liuke's city is nearly taken, but other counsels have suddenly arisen."

sentences.zh: 太祖從之。

translations.literal: Taizu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 至軍中，眾議乃決。

translations.literal: Arriving in the army, the collective deliberation was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached camp, the council's decision was settled.

sentences.zh: 斡帶急起治攻具。

translations.literal: Wo Dai hastily set about preparing siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Dai urgently prepared siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 其夜進兵攻城，遲明破之。

translations.literal: That night they advanced and assaulted the city; at dawn it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: That night they advanced to assault the city; by dawn it had fallen.

sentences.zh: 及二涅囊虎路、二蠢出路寇盜，斡帶盡平之。

translations.literal: When Ernie Nanghu Road and Erchun Chulu raided and plundered, Wo Dai entirely pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ernie Nanghu Road and Erchun Chulu turned to raiding, Wo Dai pacified them entirely.

sentences.zh: 康宗二年甲申，蘇濱水諸部不聽命，康宗使斡帶等往治其事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangzong, jia-shen, the clans along the Subin River would not obey orders; Kangzong sent Wo Dai and others to settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangzong year 2, jia-shen, the Subin River clans refused obedience; Kangzong sent Wo Dai and others to deal with them.

sentences.zh: 行次活羅海川撒阿村，召諸部。

translations.literal: Stopping at Sa'a Village on the Huoluo Sea River, he summoned the clans.
translations.idiomatic: Halting at Sa'a Village on the Huoluo Sea River, he summoned the clans.

sentences.zh: 諸部皆至，惟含國部斡豁勃堇不至。

translations.literal: All the clans came; only Han'guo clan Wohuo Bolie did not come.
translations.idiomatic: All the clans came except Wohuo Bolie of the Han'guo clan.

sentences.zh: 斡准部狄庫德勃堇、職德部廝故速勃堇亦皆遁去，遇塢塔于馬紀嶺，塢塔遂執二人以降。

translations.literal: Wozhun clan Dikude Bolie and Zhide clan Sigus Bolie also all fled; encountering Wuta at Maji Ridge, Wuta thereupon seized the two men and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Dikude Bolie of the Wozhun clan and Sigus Bolie of the Zhide clan fled as well; Wuta intercepted them at Maji Ridge, seized the two, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 於是，使斡帶將後伐斡豁，募軍于蘇濱水，斡豁元聚固守，攻而拔之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Wo Dai to lead the rear in attacking Wohuo, recruited troops on the Subin River; Wohuo had originally gathered and held firm; they attacked and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Wo Dai with the rear guard against Wohuo, raised troops on the Subin River, stormed Wohuo's stronghold, and took it.

sentences.zh: 進師北琴海辟登路，攻拔泓忒城，取畔者以歸。

translations.literal: Advancing north to Beiqin Sea Bideng Road, they attacked and took Hongte City, brought back the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Marching north to Beiqin Sea Bideng Road, they stormed Hongte City and brought the rebels back in submission.

sentences.zh: 太祖于母弟中最愛斡帶。

translations.literal: Among his younger brothers by the same mother, Taizu loved Wo Dai most.
translations.idiomatic: Of all his uterine brothers, Taizu loved Wo Dai best.

sentences.zh: 斡帶歸自泓忒城，太祖以事如甯江州，欲與斡帶偕行，斡帶曰：「兵役久勞，未及息也。」

translations.literal: Wo Dai returned from Hongte City; Taizu had business at Ningjiangzhou and wished to travel with Wo Dai; Wo Dai said: "The soldiers have long labored in war and have not yet rested."
translations.idiomatic: When Wo Dai returned from Hongte City, Taizu was bound for Ningjiangzhou and wished Wo Dai to come; Wo Dai said, "The troops have been at war too long and have not yet rested."

sentences.zh: 遂不果行。

translations.literal: The journey therefore did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: The journey was not made.

sentences.zh: 太祖還，晝寐於來流水傍，夢斡帶之場圃火，禾盡焚，不可撲滅，覺而深念之，以為憂。

translations.literal: Taizu returned and dozed by the Lailiushui; he dreamed of fire in Wo Dai's farmstead enclosure — the grain all burned, unable to be extinguished; waking, he pondered it deeply and took it as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Taizu napped beside the Lailiushui and dreamed that Wo Dai's farmstead was afire and the grain all burned beyond quenching; waking, he brooded on it with deep concern.

sentences.zh: 是時，斡帶已寢疾，太祖至，聞之，過家門不下馬，徑至斡帶所問疾。

translations.literal: At this time Wo Dai was already bedridden with illness; Taizu arrived, heard of it, passed his own gate without dismounting, went straight to Wo Dai's place to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Dai was already bedridden; when Taizu arrived and heard it, he rode past his own gate without stopping and went straight to Wo Dai's sickbed.

sentences.zh: 未幾薨，年三十四。

translations.literal: Before long he died, age thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died, aged thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 太祖每哭之慟，謂人曰：「予強與之偕行，未必死也。」

translations.literal: Taizu wept bitterly for him each time, saying to people: "Had I forced him to travel with me, he might not have died."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wept bitterly each time and told others, "Had I forced him to come with me, he might not have died."

sentences.zh: 斡帶剛毅果斷，服用整肅，臨戰決策，有世祖風。

translations.literal: Wo Dai was firm, resolute, and decisive; his dress and bearing were orderly and stern; in battle he decided strategy — he had Shizu's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Dai was resolute and decisive, stern in dress and bearing; in battle he decided strategy with Shizu's own bearing.

sentences.zh: 世祖之世，軍旅之事多專任之。

translations.literal: In Shizu's era, military affairs were largely entrusted to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Shizu's time military affairs were largely entrusted to him alone.

sentences.zh: 太祖平遼，歎曰：「恨斡帶之不及見也。」

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Liao, he sighed: "I regret that Wo Dai did not live to see it."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified the Liao, he sighed, "I regret Wo Dai did not live to see it."

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追封儀同三司、魏王，諡曰定肅。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui, posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Golden Chariot with Three Honors and Wei Prince; posthumous title Ding Su.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 15 he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Master of Golden Chariot with Three Honors as Wei Prince, with the posthumous title Ding Su, "Steadfast and Reverent."

sentences.zh: 斡賽，穆宗初，斡准部族相鈔略，遣納根涅孛堇以其兵往治，納根涅擅募蘇濱水人為兵，不別的，輒攻略之。

translations.literal: Wo Sai, at the beginning of Muzong, the Wozhun clan mutually plundered; Nagen Nie Bolie was sent with his troops to settle it; Nagen Nie on his own authority recruited Subin River people as troops, without distinguishing targets, and straightway raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Muzong's reign the Wozhun clan preyed on one another; Nagen Nie Bolie was dispatched with troops to restore order; he took it on himself to raise Subin River men as soldiers and, without distinction, raided and plundered.

sentences.zh: 其人來告，穆宗使斡賽及冶訶往問狀。

translations.literal: The people came to report; Muzong sent Wo Sai and Yehe to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the victims complained, Muzong sent Wo Sai and Yehe to investigate.

sentences.zh: 納根涅雖伏而不肯亻賞所取，因遁去。

translations.literal: Nagen Nie though submitting would not compensate for what he had taken, and therefore fled.
translations.idiomatic: Nagen Nie submitted but refused to return what he had plundered and fled.

sentences.zh: 冶訶等皆不欲追，斡賽督軍而進。

translations.literal: Yehe and the others all did not wish to pursue; Wo Sai pressed the army forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yehe and the others did not wish to pursue; Wo Sai drove the army forward.

sentences.zh: 至把忽嶺西毛密水，及之，大破其眾，納根涅死焉。

translations.literal: Reaching Maomishui west of Bahu Ridge, they caught up, greatly broke their force; Nagen Nie died there.
translations.idiomatic: West of Bahu Ridge at Maomishui they overtook him, routed his force, and Nagen Nie was killed.

sentences.zh: 斡賽撫定蘇濱水民部，執納根涅之母及其妻子而歸。

translations.literal: Wo Sai pacified the Subin River people's clans, seized Nagen Nie's mother and his wife and children, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Sai pacified the Subin River clans, seized Nagen Nie's mother, wife, and children, and returned.

sentences.zh: 穆宗曰：「斡賽年尚幼，已能集事，可嘉也。」

translations.literal: Muzong said: "Wo Sai is still young yet already able to gather affairs — it is commendable."
translations.idiomatic: Muzong said, "Wo Sai is still young, yet he already brings matters to completion — worthy of praise."

sentences.zh: 康宗二年甲申，斡帶治蘇濱水諸部，斡賽、斡魯佐之，定諸部而還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangzong, jia-shen, Wo Dai settled the Subin River clans; Wo Sai and Wo Lu assisted him; the clans were settled and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangzong year 2, jia-shen, Wo Dai settled the Subin River clans with Wo Sai and Wo Lu assisting; when the clans were pacified they returned.

sentences.zh: 久之，高麗殺行人阿聒、勝昆，而築九城於曷懶甸。

translations.literal: After a long while, Goryeo killed the envoys Azuo and Shengkun, and built nine fortresses in Helan.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Goryeo killed the envoys Azuo and Shengkun and built nine fortresses in the Helan region.

sentences.zh: 斡賽將內外兵，劾古活你茁、蒲察狄古乃佐之。

translations.literal: Wo Sai commanded inner and outer troops; Heguonizhuo and Pucha Digunai assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Sai took command of inner and outer troops, with Heguonizhuo and Pucha Digunai as his lieutenants.

sentences.zh: 高麗兵數萬來拒，斡賽分兵為十隊，更出迭人，遂大破之。

translations.literal: Goryeo troops in the tens of thousands came to resist; Wo Sai divided his forces into ten squads, rotating squads in relief, and utterly routed them.
translations.idiomatic: When tens of thousands of Goryeo troops came to resist, Wo Sai divided his army into ten squads and rotated them in relief until he routed the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 斡賽母和你隈疾篤，召還，以斡魯代之。

translations.literal: Wo Sai's mother Heniwei fell gravely ill; he was recalled, and Wo Lu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo Sai's mother Heniwei fell gravely ill, he was recalled and Wo Lu took his place.

sentences.zh: 未幾，斡賽複至軍，再破高麗軍，進圍其城。

translations.literal: Before long Wo Sai again reached the army, again defeated Goryeo's troops, and advanced to besiege their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wo Sai returned to the front, defeated the Goryeo army again, and advanced to besiege their fortresses.

sentences.zh: 七月，高麗請和，盡歸前後亡命及所侵故地，退九城之戍，遂與之和。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Goryeo sued for peace, fully returning fugitives from before and after and encroached former territory, withdrawing garrisons from the nine fortresses; peace was then made.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Goryeo sued for peace, restored all fugitives taken before and after the conflict and the territory it had seized, and withdrew the garrisons from the nine fortresses; peace was made.

sentences.zh: 皇統五年，追封衛國王。

translations.literal: In Huangtong year 5, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year 5 he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 子 宗永

translations.literal: Son: Zongyong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zongyong

sentences.zh: 宗永，本名挑撻，斡賽子。

translations.literal: Zongyong, original name Tiaota, was Wo Sai's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyong, whose original name was Tiaota, was the son of Wo Sai.

sentences.zh: 長身美髯，忠確勇毅。

translations.literal: Tall of stature with a fine beard, loyal, resolute, brave, and steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and bearded, he was loyal, resolute, brave, and steadfast.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，以宗室子預誅宗磐，擢甯遠大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan, as a prince's son he took part in executing Zongpan and was promoted to General of Pacifying the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjuan, as a member of the imperial clan he took part in the execution of Zongpan and was promoted to General of Pacifying the Distant.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，充牌印祗候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong, served as attendant of seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Huangtong he served as attendant of seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為趙州刺史，秩滿再任，轉興平軍節度使，改大名尹。

translations.literal: In year 5, sent out as prefect of Zhaozhou; at term's end reappointed; transferred to military commissioner of Xingping Army; changed to grand prefect of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was posted as prefect of Zhaozhou, reappointed at the end of his term, then made military commissioner of Xingping Army and grand prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，複為興平軍節度使，曆昭德軍、臨洮、鳳翔尹。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan year 3, again made military commissioner of Xingping Army; successively held Zhao De Army, Lintao, and grand prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 3 he again became military commissioner of Xingping Army and successively served at Zhao De Army, Lintao, and as grand prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，入為工部尚書，與蘇保衡、完顏餘里也遷加伐宋士官賞。

translations.literal: In Dading year 2, entered service as Minister of Works; with Su Baoheng and Wanyan Yuli promoted and rewarded officers for the campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading year 2 he entered court as Minister of Works and, with Su Baoheng and Wanyan Yuli, promoted and rewarded officers who had fought against Song.

sentences.zh: 宋永性滯不習事，凡與土賊戰者一概加之。

translations.literal: Zongyong was dull and inexperienced in affairs; to all who had fought local bandits he indiscriminately granted rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyong was slow-witted and inexperienced; he indiscriminately rewarded everyone who had fought local bandits.

sentences.zh: 世宗久乃知之，謂宰相曰：「若一概追還，必生怨望。

translations.literal: Shizong only learned of this after a long time and said to the chief ministers: "If we recover all rewards uniformly, resentment will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long while did Shizong learn of this and tell the chief ministers, "If we recover all the rewards at once, resentment is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 若因循不問，則爵賞濫矣。

translations.literal: If we let it pass without inquiry, titles and rewards will be abused.
translations.idiomatic: If we let the matter pass without inquiry, titles and rewards will be debased.

sentences.zh: 其與土賊戰者，有能以寡敵眾，一人敵三十人以上者，依已遷為定。」

translations.literal: For those who fought local bandits: those who could use the few against the many, one man matching thirty or more — let their already received promotions stand.
translations.idiomatic: As for those who had fought local bandits, anyone who had used the few against the many — one man matching thirty or more — would keep the rank already granted him.

sentences.zh: 改同簽大宗正事、震武軍節度使，卒。

translations.literal: Changed to co-signatory of the Grand Imperial Clan Office and military commissioner of Zhenwu Army; died.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as co-signatory of the Grand Imperial Clan Office and military commissioner of Zhenwu Army, and later died.

sentences.zh: 斡者，天會十五年大封宗室，追封魯王，正隆例改封公。

translations.literal: Wo Zhe: in Tianhui year 15 during the great enfeoffment of the imperial clan, posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lu; under the Zhenglong precedent changed to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Zhe was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lu during the great enfeoffment of the imperial clan in Tianhui year 15; under the Zhenglong precedent the title was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 孫 璋

translations.literal: Grandson: Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Zhang

sentences.zh: 子神土懣，驃騎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: His son Shen Tuman, senior general of the Flying Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen Tuman was a senior general of the Flying Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 子璋本名胡麻愈，多勇略，通女直、契丹、漢字。

translations.literal: Zhang, original name Humayu, very brave and resourceful, versed in Jurchen, Khitan, and Chinese script.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, whose original name was Humayu, was bold and resourceful and could read Jurchen, Khitan, and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 年十八，左副元帥撒離喝引在麾下。

translations.literal: At eighteen the Left Deputy Marshal Salihu took him under his command.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was taken into the service of Left Deputy Marshal Salihu.

sentences.zh: 以事如京師，見梁王宗弼與語，宗弼悅之。

translations.literal: On business at the capital he met Prince of Liang Zongbi and spoke with him; Zongbi was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: While at the capital on official business he met Prince of Liang Zongbi and spoke with him; Zongbi took a liking to him.

sentences.zh: 皇統六年，父神土懣卒，宗弼奏璋可襲謀克，詔從之。

translations.literal: Huangtong year 6, his father Shen Tuman died; Zongbi memorialized that Zhang could inherit the meng'an post; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year 6 his father Shen Tuman died; Zongbi memorialized that Zhang should inherit the meng'an post, and the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，充牌印祗候，以罪免，奪其謀克，寓居中都。

translations.literal: Tiande year 3, served as attendant of seals and credentials; dismissed for a crime, stripped of his meng'an, and lived at the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande year 3 he served as attendant of seals and credentials, but was dismissed for a crime, stripped of his meng'an, and took up residence at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 璋以殺沙離只自攝同知留守，世宗因而授之，心常不自安，遂與兵部尚書可喜謀，因世宗謁山陵作亂。

translations.literal: Zhang, having killed Shalizhi, on his own authority assumed the acting post of associate director of garrison administration; Shizong thereupon appointed him, but he was never at ease and conspired with Minister of War Kexi to rebel when Shizong visited the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Shalizhi, Zhang took the acting post of associate director of garrison administration on his own authority; Shizong confirmed the appointment, but Zhang never felt secure and conspired with Minister of War Kexi to rebel when Shizong visited the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，上謁山陵，璋等九人會於可喜家，說萬戶高松，不從。

translations.literal: Dading year 2, when the emperor visited the tombs, Zhang and eight others met at Kexi's house and tried to persuade wanhu Gao Song, who refused.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading year 2, when the emperor visited the tombs, Zhang and eight others met at Kexi's house and tried to win over wanhu Gao Song, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 璋知事不成，乃與可喜共執斡論詣有司陳，上誅可喜、李惟忠等，以璋為彰化軍節度使。

translations.literal: Zhang knew the plot would fail; he and Kexi together seized Wolun and went to the authorities to report; the emperor executed Kexi, Li Weizhong, and others, and made Zhang military commissioner of Zhanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the plot would fail, Zhang and Kexi seized Wolun and reported the conspiracy to the authorities; the emperor executed Kexi, Li Weizhong, and the others, and made Zhang military commissioner of Zhanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 宋將吳璘出散關，據寶雞以西，詔璋赴元帥都監徒單合喜軍前任使。

translations.literal: Song general Wu Lin came out through San'guan Pass and held the region west of Baoji; Zhang was ordered to proceed to Marshal Supervisor Tudan Hexi's army as advance officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Song general Wu Lin came out through San'guan Pass and seized the region west of Baoji, Zhang was ordered to join Marshal Supervisor Tudan Hexi's army as advance officer.

sentences.zh: 於是，宋人據原州，甯州刺史顏盞門都以兵四千攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Then the Song held Yuanzhou; Ningzhou prefect Yanshan Mendu attacked with four thousand troops but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Song then held Yuanzhou; Ningzhou prefect Yanshan Mendu attacked with four thousand men but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 宋將姚良輔以兵十萬至原州，權副統完顏習尼列以千騎援門都兵，而姚良輔兵多，諸將皆不敢與戰。

translations.literal: Song general Yao Liangfu arrived at Yuanzhou with a hundred thousand troops; acting deputy supreme commander Wanyan Xini Lie came with a thousand horsemen to reinforce Mendu's troops, but Yao Liangfu's force was large and none of the generals dared fight.
translations.idiomatic: Song general Yao Liangfu reached Yuanzhou with a hundred thousand troops; acting deputy supreme commander Wanyan Xini Lie came with a thousand cavalry to reinforce Mendu, but Yao Liangfu's army was too large and none of the Jin generals dared give battle.

sentences.zh: 及璋至軍，會平涼、涇州、潘原、長武等戍兵，合二萬人。

translations.literal: When Zhang reached the army, he gathered garrison troops from Pingliang, Jingzhou, Panyuan, Changwu, and elsewhere — twenty thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang reached the front, he assembled garrison troops from Pingliang, Jingzhou, Panyuan, Changwu, and elsewhere, twenty thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 璋使押軍猛安石抹許里阿補以兵二千軍於城北，習尼列以兵三千軍於城西北十里麥子原，皆據高阜為陣。

translations.literal: Zhang sent escort-army meng'an Shimo Xulibu with two thousand troops to camp north of the city; Xini Lie with three thousand camped at Maizi Plain ten li northwest of the city; both took high ground for their formations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang posted escort-army meng'an Shimo Xulibu with two thousand men north of the city and Xini Lie with three thousand at Maizi Plain ten li to the northwest; both drew up on high ground.

sentences.zh: 璋以本部兵陣於城西。

translations.literal: Zhang arrayed his own troops west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang drew up his own troops west of the city.

sentences.zh: 姚良輔出自北嶺，先遣萬人攻許里阿補，自以軍九萬陣麥子原下，捍以劍盾、行馬，外列騎士，步卒居其中，敢死士鎖足行馬間，持大刀為拒，分為八陣，而別以騎二千襲璋軍。

translations.literal: Yao Liangfu came out from North Ridge; first sent ten thousand to attack Xulibu; himself with ninety thousand arrayed below Maizi Plain, shielded by sword-shields and war wagons, cavalry outside, infantry within, dare-to-die troops chained between the war wagons holding great swords as barrier, divided into eight formations; and separately sent two thousand cavalry to strike Zhang's army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Liangfu came out from North Ridge and first sent ten thousand men against Xulibu; he himself deployed ninety thousand below Maizi Plain behind sword-shields and war wagons, cavalry on the outside and infantry within, with dare-to-die troops chained between the war wagons wielding great swords as a barrier, in eight formations; he also sent two thousand cavalry separately to strike Zhang's army.

sentences.zh: 璋方出迎戰，習尼列來報曰：「宋之重兵皆在麥子原矣。」

translations.literal: Zhang was just sallying to meet the fight when Xini Lie came to report: "Song's main force is all at Maizi Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was just riding out to meet the enemy when Xini Lie reported, "Song's main force is all at Maizi Plain.

sentences.zh: 璋遣萬戶特里失烏也以押軍猛安奚慶喜、照撒兵二千援許里阿補，遣撒屋出、崔尹以兵二千益習尼列。

translations.literal: Zhang sent wanhu Telisiwuye with escort meng'an Xi Qingxi and Zhasa troops of two thousand to aid Xulibu; sent Sawuchu and Cui Yin with two thousand to reinforce Xini Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sent wanhu Telisiwuye with escort meng'an Xi Qingxi and two thousand Zhasa troops to aid Xulibu, and Sawuchu and Cui Yin with two thousand men to reinforce Xini Lie.

sentences.zh: 許里阿補與宋人接戰，良久，敗之。

translations.literal: Xulibu joined battle with the Song; after a long fight, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xulibu engaged the Song and, after a long fight, routed them.

sentences.zh: 宋兵在麥子原者最堅，習尼列與移刺補、奧屯撒屋出、崔尹、僕根撒屈出以兵五千沿壕為狀，餘兵皆舍馬步戰，擊其前行騎士，走之。

translations.literal: The Song troops at Maizi Plain were the stoutest; Xini Lie with Yiliebu, Aotun Sawuchu, Cui Yin, and Pugensaquchu with five thousand along the moat in feint formation; the rest dismounted for foot combat, struck their forward cavalry, and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song force at Maizi Plain was the stoutest; Xini Lie with Yiliebu, Aotun Sawuchu, Cui Yin, and Pugensaquchu feinted along the moat with five thousand men while the rest dismounted and, fighting on foot, broke the Song vanguard cavalry and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 於是，行馬以前沖以長槍，行馬以後射以勁弓。

translations.literal: Then the war wagons in front charged with long spears; those behind shot with powerful bows.
translations.idiomatic: The war wagons in front charged with long spears while those behind rained arrows from powerful bows.

sentences.zh: 良輔兵稍挫，習尼列乘勝麾兵，撤其行馬，破其七陣。

translations.literal: Liangfu's troops faltered slightly; Xini Lie seized victory and waved his troops forward, pulled away their war wagons, and broke seven of their formations.
translations.idiomatic: As Liangfu's line began to buckle, Xini Lie pressed the advantage, tore away their war wagons, and broke seven formations.

sentences.zh: 良輔複整兵出，習尼列少卻，而璋已破城下宋兵，與習尼列會。

translations.literal: Liangfu regrouped and came out again; Xini Lie retreated slightly, but Zhang had already defeated the Song below the city and joined Xini Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu regrouped and came out again; Xini Lie fell back slightly, but Zhang had already routed the Song below the walls and joined him.

sentences.zh: 使僕根以伏兵擊良輔。

translations.literal: He sent Pugen with hidden troops to strike Liangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pugen with an ambush to strike Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 習尼列亦整兵與戰，奮擊之，大破良輔軍，斬首萬餘級，墜壕死者不可勝數，鎖足行馬者盡殪之，獲甲二萬餘，器仗稱是。

translations.literal: Xini Lie also regrouped and fought, pressing the attack hard; utterly routed Liangfu's army; heads cut exceeded ten thousand; those who fell into moats and died were beyond counting; those chained between war wagons were all slain; captured armor over twenty thousand sets; weapons and gear in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Xini Lie regrouped and pressed the attack, routing Liangfu's army completely; more than ten thousand heads were taken, countless men fell into the moats and died, and every dare-to-die soldier chained between the war wagons was killed; they captured more than twenty thousand suits of armor and weapons in proportion.

sentences.zh: 良輔亦中兩創脫去。

translations.literal: Liangfu also took two wounds and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu himself took two wounds and escaped.

sentences.zh: 遂圍原州，穴其西城，城圮，宋人宵遁。

translations.literal: They then besieged Yuanzhou, undermined the west wall; the wall collapsed; the Song fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: They then besieged Yuanzhou, undermined the west wall until it collapsed, and the Song fled by night.

sentences.zh: 璋等入原州。

translations.literal: Zhang and the others entered Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and his officers entered Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋戍軍在寶雞以西，聞之皆自散關遁去。

translations.literal: Song garrison troops west of Baoji, hearing this, all fled through San'guan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song garrisons west of Baoji heard the news, they all fled back through San'guan Pass.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹烏延蒲離黑、丹州刺史赤盞胡速魯改已去德順州，宋吳璘複據之，都監合喜以璋權都統，與習尼列將兵二萬救德順。

translations.literal: Capital prefect Wuyan Pulühei and Danzhou prefect Chizan Husulugai had already left Deshun; Song Wu Lin again seized it; supervisor Hexi made Zhang acting supreme commander; with Xini Lie led twenty thousand to relieve Deshun.
translations.idiomatic: Capital prefect Wuyan Pulühei and Danzhou prefect Chizan Husulugai had already withdrawn from Deshun when Song general Wu Lin seized it again; supervisor Hexi made Zhang acting supreme commander and, with Xini Lie, led twenty thousand men to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 璋率騎兵前行，與璘騎拴二萬戰于張義堡遂沙山下，敗之，追北四十餘里。

translations.literal: Zhang led cavalry forward and with Wu Lin's twenty thousand cavalry fought at Zhangyibao below Suishashan; defeated them and pursued north over forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang led the cavalry forward and defeated Wu Lin's twenty thousand horsemen below Suishashan at Zhangyibao, then pursued them north for more than forty li.

sentences.zh: 璘軍遇隘不得前，斬首數十級。

translations.literal: Wu Lin's army met narrow terrain and could not advance; several dozen heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin's army was blocked by narrow passes and could not advance; the Jin forces cut down several dozen men.

sentences.zh: 璋至德順，璘據城北險要為營，璋亦策營與璘相望，可三里許。

translations.literal: Zhang reached Deshun; Wu Lin held the north of the city at perilous ground for a camp; Zhang also pitched camp facing Wu Lin, about three li apart.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang reached Deshun, Wu Lin had encamped on the perilous ground north of the city; Zhang pitched camp facing him, about three li away.

sentences.zh: 兩軍遇於城東，凡五接戰，璘軍敗走，璋追至城下。

translations.literal: The two armies met east of the city; five engagements in all; Wu Lin's army was defeated and fled; Zhang pursued to the foot of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies clashed east of the city in five engagements; Wu Lin's army was beaten and fled, and Zhang pursued to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 璘軍已據城北岡阜，與其城上兵相應，以弩夾射璋軍。

translations.literal: Wu Lin's army had already held the north hill ridge and coordinated with troops on the walls, shooting at Zhang's army with crossbows from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin's troops had already seized the ridge north of the city and, coordinating with the defenders on the walls, raked Zhang's army with crossbow fire from both sides.

sentences.zh: 璋軍陽卻，城中出兵來追，璋反施與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Zhang's army feigned retreat; troops from the city came out in pursuit; Zhang turned and fought, routing them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's army feigned retreat; when troops sallied from the city in pursuit, he wheeled about and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 合喜遣統軍都監泥河以兵七千來會，與璘軍複戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Hexi sent army supervisor Nihe with seven thousand to join; again fought Wu Lin's army and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi sent army supervisor Nihe with seven thousand men to join the fight; they engaged Wu Lin again and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 璘遣兵據東山堡，欲樹柵，璋與習尼列、泥河議曰：「敵若據東山堡，此城亦不可拔，宜急擊之。」

translations.literal: Wu Lin sent troops to hold Dongshan Fort, intending to build palisades; Zhang with Xini Lie and Nihe deliberated: "If the enemy holds Dongshan Fort, this city too cannot be taken; we should strike quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin sent troops to hold Dongshan Fort and began building palisades; Zhang, Xini Lie, and Nihe agreed: "If the enemy holds Dongshan Fort, this city cannot be taken either; we must strike at once.

sentences.zh: 於是璋先據要地，習尼列以兵逼東山堡，璘兵恃濠相拒，短兵接，璘兵退走，習尼列追擊之。

translations.literal: Zhang first seized key ground; Xini Lie pressed Dongshan Fort with troops; Wu Lin's men relied on the moat to resist; at close quarters Wu Lin's troops retreated; Xini Lie pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang seized the key ground first; Xini Lie pressed Dongshan Fort while Wu Lin's men held behind the moat; after close combat Wu Lin's troops broke and Xini Lie pursued.

sentences.zh: 璘城北營兵可六千人，登北岡來戰，璋之漢軍少卻，傷者二百人。

translations.literal: Wu Lin's north camp had about six thousand; they climbed the north ridge to fight; Zhang's Han soldiers retreated slightly; two hundred wounded.
translations.idiomatic: About six thousand men from Wu Lin's northern camp climbed the north ridge to fight; Zhang's Han troops fell back slightly and two hundred were wounded.

sentences.zh: 璘遂焚璋軍攻城具，璋率移刺補猛安兵逾北岡擊走之。

translations.literal: Wu Lin then burned Zhang's siege equipment; Zhang led Yiliebu's meng'an troops over the north ridge and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin then burned Zhang's siege equipment; Zhang led meng'an Yiliebu's troops over the north ridge and drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 璘軍隔小塹射璋軍，移刺補少卻，習尼列望見北原火發，乃止攻東山堡，亟與將士來赴，引善射者先登，率劉安漢軍三百人擊敗之。

translations.literal: Wu Lin's army across a small trench shot at Zhang's army; Yiliebu retreated slightly; Xini Lie saw fire on the north plain, halted the attack on Dongshan Fort, hurried with officers and men; led good archers to advance first; with Liu An's three hundred Han troops defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin's troops fired from across a small trench and Yiliebu fell back; seeing fire on the north plain, Xini Lie broke off the attack on Dongshan Fort and rushed to help, sending skilled archers forward first and, with Liu An's three hundred Han troops, defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 璘軍皆走險，璘以軍三萬據險作三陣，皆環以劍盾、行馬。
