translations.literal: Wu Lin's troops all fled to perilous ground; Wu Lin with thirty thousand made three formations on difficult terrain, all ringed with sword-shields and war wagons.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin's troops all fled to difficult ground; he drew up thirty thousand men in three formations on the heights, each ringed with sword-shields and war wagons.

sentences.zh: 璋遣萬戶石抹迭勒由別路自後擊之，特里失烏也、移刺補以二千人當其前，以強弓射之，璘兵大敗，墮溝壑者甚眾。

translations.literal: Zhang sent wanhu Shimo Dielü by another route to strike from behind; Telisiwuye and Yiliebu with two thousand blocked them in front; shot with powerful bows; Wu Lin's troops were greatly defeated; many fell into ditches and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sent wanhu Shimo Dielü by a separate route to strike from the rear while Telisiwuye and Yiliebu with two thousand men blocked the front and raked them with powerful bows; Wu Lin's army was routed and many fell into ditches and ravines.

sentences.zh: 璋軍度澗追之，斬數千級而還。

translations.literal: Zhang's army crossed a stream in pursuit, cut several thousand heads, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's army crossed a stream in pursuit, cut down several thousand men, and returned.

sentences.zh: 璘軍雖敗，猶恃其眾，都監合喜使武威軍副總管夾古查刺來問策。

translations.literal: Though Wu Lin's army was defeated, they still relied on their numbers; supervisor Hexi sent Wujun deputy commander Jiagu Zhaci to ask for strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Though defeated, Wu Lin still relied on his numbers; supervisor Hexi sent Wujun deputy commander Jiagu Zhaci to ask Zhang's counsel.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「吳璘恃險，不善野戰，我退軍平涼，彼必棄險就平地，然後可圖也。」

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Wu Lin relies on terrain; he is not skilled in field battle; if we withdraw to Pingliang, he will surely abandon the perilous ground for level ground; then he can be dealt with.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said, "Wu Lin relies on terrain and is poor at open battle; if we withdraw to Pingliang, he will abandon the heights for level ground, and then we can deal with him.

sentences.zh: 璋曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhang said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 彼恃其眾，非特恃險也。

translations.literal: He relies on his numbers — not only on terrain.
translations.idiomatic: He relies on his numbers, not on terrain alone.

sentences.zh: 昔人有言，'寧棄千軍，不棄寸地'，故退兵不如濟師。

translations.literal: Ancients said, 'Better abandon a thousand troops than an inch of ground' — therefore withdrawing is inferior to reinforcing.
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said, 'Better lose a thousand troops than an inch of ground' — withdrawal is worse than sending reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 我退軍平涼，彼軍深入吾地，固壘以拒我，則如之何。」

translations.literal: If we withdraw to Pingliang and their army penetrates deep into our territory and fortifies to resist us — what then?
translations.idiomatic: If we withdraw to Pingliang and their army pushes deep into our territory and fortifies against us, what then?

sentences.zh: 查刺還報，合喜於是親率四萬人赴之。

translations.literal: Zhaci returned to report; Hexi thereupon personally led forty thousand to join.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaci returned with the report, and Hexi personally led forty thousand men to join the fight.

sentences.zh: 吳璘詰旦乘陰霧晦冥分兵四道來襲，戰於城東，離而複合者數四。

translations.literal: Wu Lin at dawn used dark fog and murk to divide into four columns and attack; fought east of the city; separated and rejoined four times.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Wu Lin used thick fog to divide his force into four columns and attack east of the city; the battle broke and re-formed four times.

sentences.zh: 漢軍千戶李展率麾下兵先登奮擊之，璘軍陣動。

translations.literal: Han-army chiliarch Li Zhan led his troops to scale first and strike fiercely; Wu Lin's formation wavered.
translations.idiomatic: Han-army chiliarch Li Zhan led his men forward in the first assault; Wu Lin's line wavered.

sentences.zh: 璋乘勝踵擊，璘軍複敗，追至北岡，璘走險，璋急擊之，殺略殆盡。

translations.literal: Zhang pressed the victory in pursuit; Wu Lin's army was again defeated; pursued to North Ridge; Wu Lin fled to perilous ground; Zhang pressed hard; killed and plundered nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang pressed the victory in pursuit; Wu Lin's army broke again; pursued to North Ridge, Wu Lin fled to difficult ground, and Zhang pressed hard until nearly all were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 璘分半軍守秦州，合喜駐軍水洛城東，自六盤山至石山頭分兵守之，斷其餉道。

translations.literal: Wu Lin split half his army to hold Qinzhou; Hexi camped east of Shuilo City; from Liupan Mountains to Shishantou divided troops to hold positions, cutting their supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin left half his army to hold Qinzhou; Hexi encamped east of Shuilo City and posted troops from Liupan Mountains to Shishantou, cutting the enemy supply line.

sentences.zh: 璘乃引歸。

translations.literal: Wu Lin then withdrew homeward.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宋經略使荊皋以步騎三萬自德順西去，璋以兵八千、習尼列以兵五千追擊之。

translations.literal: Song frontier commissioner Jing Gao with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry went west from Deshun; Zhang with eight thousand and Xini Lie with five thousand pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Song frontier commissioner Jing Gao withdrew west from Deshun with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry; Zhang with eight thousand men and Xini Lie with five thousand pursued.

sentences.zh: 習尼列兵乃出其前，還自赤觜，遇其前鋒，敗之于高赤崖下。

translations.literal: Xini Lie's troops got ahead of them; returning from Chizui, met their vanguard and defeated them below Gaochiya Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: Xini Lie's troops got ahead of them; coming back from Chizui, he met their vanguard and defeated them below Gaochiya Cliff.

sentences.zh: 複與其中軍戰，自日昃至暮，乃罷。

translations.literal: Again fought their center army; from mid-afternoon to dusk before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He fought their center army again from mid-afternoon until dusk before breaking off.

sentences.zh: 荊皋乘夜來襲營，為退軍八十里。

translations.literal: Jing Gao used the night to raid the camp; the army was pushed back eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Gao raided the camp by night and forced a retreat of eighty li.

sentences.zh: 明日，習尼列追之。

translations.literal: Next day Xini Lie pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xini Lie pursued.

sentences.zh: 璋兵至上八節，宋兵據險為陣，璋舍馬步戰，地險不得接，相拒至曙。

translations.literal: Zhang's troops reached Shangbajie; Song troops held perilous ground in formation; Zhang dismounted for foot combat; terrain too perilous to engage; stood off until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's troops reached Shangbajie, where the Song held difficult ground in formation; Zhang dismounted to fight on foot, but the terrain was too steep to close; the two sides faced off until dawn.

sentences.zh: 宋兵勸，璋乘之，追至甘穀城，習尼列兵亦至，宋兵宵遁，璋遂班師。

translations.literal: Song troops wavered; Zhang seized the moment; pursued to Gangu City; Xini Lie's troops also arrived; Song fled by night; Zhang then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song line wavered, Zhang pressed the advantage and pursued to Gangu City; Xini Lie's troops also arrived, the Song fled by night, and Zhang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 習尼列追至伏羌城，不及而還。

translations.literal: Xini Lie pursued to Fuxiang City but did not catch up and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xini Lie pursued as far as Fuxiang City but failed to overtake the enemy and turned back.

sentences.zh: 上使禦史中丞達吉視諸軍功狀，達吉舊與璋有隙，故損其功。

translations.literal: The emperor sent censor-in-chief Daji to review all army merit reports; Daji had old grievances with Zhang and therefore reduced his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent censor-in-chief Daji to review the army merit reports; Daji had old grievances with Zhang and deliberately understated his achievements.

sentences.zh: 詔璋將士賞比諸軍半之，璋兼陝西路都統，進官一階。

translations.literal: Edict: Zhang's officers and men rewarded at half other armies' rate; Zhang additionally made supreme commander of Shaanxi Circuit; one rank promotion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Zhang's officers and men half the rewards given other armies; Zhang was also made supreme commander of Shaanxi Circuit and promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 及元帥府上功，璋居多，詔達吉削官兩階，杖八十，解職。

translations.literal: When the marshal's headquarters submitted merit reports, Zhang's share was largest; edict stripped Daji two ranks, eighty blows with the stick, dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the marshal's headquarters submitted its merit reports, Zhang's share was the largest; the emperor stripped Daji of two ranks, had him beaten eighty blows, and dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 上複賞璋及將士如諸軍，以璋為西北路招討使。

translations.literal: The emperor again rewarded Zhang and his troops like other armies; made Zhang commissioner for pacification of the Northwest Route.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then rewarded Zhang and his troops on the same scale as the other armies and made Zhang commissioner for pacification of the Northwest Route.

sentences.zh: 召為元帥左都監，兼安化軍節度使，賜以弓矢衣帶佩刀。

translations.literal: Summoned as left marshal supervisor; concurrently military commissioner of Anhua Army; granted bow, arrows, robes, belt, and sword.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as left marshal supervisor and concurrently military commissioner of Anhua Army, and was granted a bow, arrows, robes, belt, and sword.

sentences.zh: 改益都尹，左都監如故。

translations.literal: Changed to grand prefect of Yidu; left marshal supervisor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand prefect of Yidu while retaining the post of left marshal supervisor.

sentences.zh: 宋人棄海州遁去，焚官民廬舍且盡。

translations.literal: Song abandoned Haizhou and fled, burning nearly all official and private buildings.
translations.idiomatic: The Song abandoned Haizhou and fled, burning nearly all government and private buildings.

sentences.zh: 璋至海州，得所棄糧三萬六千余石，安集其人，複其屯戍。

translations.literal: Zhang reached Haizhou; recovered abandoned grain of over thirty-six thousand shi; settled the people; restored garrison colonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang reached Haizhou, he recovered more than thirty-six thousand shi of abandoned grain, resettled the people, and restored the garrison colonies.

sentences.zh: 五年，宋人約和，罷三路都統，複置陝西路統軍司，璋為統軍使。

translations.literal: Year 5, Song made peace; abolished the three-route supreme commands; restored Shaanxi Circuit army supervisorate; Zhang made army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the Song made peace; the three-route supreme commands were abolished, the Shaanxi Circuit army supervisorate was restored, and Zhang was made army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「監軍合喜年老，故授卿此職。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Supervisor Hexi is old, therefore I appoint you to this post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Supervisor Hexi is old, so I am giving you this post.

sentences.zh: 邊境無事，且召卿矣。」

translations.literal: When the border is quiet I shall summon you back.
translations.idiomatic: When the border is quiet I shall summon you back.

sentences.zh: 以本官兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: Made him concurrently grand prefect of Jingzhao with his existing title.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made grand prefect of Jingzhao while retaining his existing title.

sentences.zh: 召為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Summoned as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 璋奏：「竊觀文武百官有相為朋黨者，今在台自臣外無女直人，乞不限資考，量材奏擬。」

translations.literal: Zhang memorialized: "I have observed that civil and military officials form factions with one another; at the Censorate today, apart from myself, there are no Jurchen men. I beg that qualification and seniority not be limiting factors, and that candidates be recommended according to talent."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang memorialized: "I see civil and military officials forming factions. At the Censorate today there is not a single Jurchen apart from me. I ask that you not limit appointments by seniority or examination rank, but recommend men according to their ability."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朋黨為誰，即糾治之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Whoever the factions are, investigate and punish them at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Name the factions and prosecute them at once.

sentences.zh: 朕選女直人，未得其人，豈以資考為限，論其人材而已。」

translations.literal: In selecting Jurchen men I have not yet found the right people — how could I be bound by qualification and seniority? I judge only by talent."
translations.idiomatic: I have not yet found the Jurchen men I need. Why should I be bound by rank and seniority? I judge men by talent alone."

sentences.zh: 頃之，璋奏曰：「太祖武元皇帝受天明命，太宗皇帝奄定宋土，自古帝王之興，必稱受命，當制'大金受命之寶'，以明示萬世。」

translations.literal: Shortly after, Zhang memorialized: "Taizu the Martial Founder received Heaven's bright mandate; Taizong swiftly settled Song territory. Since antiquity the rise of emperors has always been called receiving the mandate — we should cast the 'Great Jin Seal of Received Mandate' to make it clear to ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Zhang memorialized again: "Taizu the Martial Founder received Heaven's mandate, and Taizong swiftly pacified Song soil. Every dynastic founding is proclaimed as receiving the mandate. We should cast the Great Jin Seal of Received Mandate to proclaim it to all posterity."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言正合朕意。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words match my intent exactly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your words match my intent exactly."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使夏國市玉，十八年，受命寶成，奏告天地宗廟社稷，上禦正殿。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to Western Xia to purchase jade; in the eighteenth year the Mandate Seal was completed, reports were made to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain, and the emperor took his seat in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Western Xia to buy jade. In year 18 the Mandate Seal was finished. He reported to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain, and took his seat in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改大興尹，為賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was changed to grand prefect of Daxing and made envoy to congratulate Song on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he became grand prefect of Daxing and envoy to congratulate Song on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 璋受命使宋，即行，上遣人馳諭璋曰：「宋人若不遵舊禮，慎勿付書。

translations.literal: Zhang received his commission as envoy to Song and set out; the emperor sent a rider to instruct him: "If the Song do not observe the old rites, be careful not to hand over the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang received his commission and set out. The emperor sent a rider ahead with orders: "If the Song do not observe the old rites, do not hand over the letter.

sentences.zh: 如不令卿等入見，即持書歸。

translations.literal: If they do not allow you to have an audience, take the letter and return.
translations.idiomatic: If they refuse you an audience, take the letter and return.

sentences.zh: 若迫而取之，亦勿赴宴，其回書及禮物一切勿受。」

translations.literal: If they force it from you, still do not attend banquets; their reply letters and gifts — accept none of them."
translations.idiomatic: If they force the letter from you, still do not attend their banquets, and accept no reply or gift of any kind."

sentences.zh: 璋至臨安，宋人請以太子接書，不從。

translations.literal: Zhang reached Lin'an; the Song asked that the crown prince receive the letter — he refused.
translations.idiomatic: At Lin'an the Song asked that the crown prince receive the letter. Zhang refused.

sentences.zh: 宋人就館迫取書，璋與之，且赴宴，多受禮物。

translations.literal: Song men came to the lodge and forced the letter from him; Zhang gave it, attended banquets, and accepted many gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Song officials came to the lodge and forced the letter from him. Zhang surrendered it, attended their banquets, and accepted many gifts.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，上怒，欲置之極刑。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported it; the emperor was angry and wished to impose the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was informed, the emperor was furious and wanted the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 左丞相良弼奏曰：「璋為將，大破宋軍，宋人仇之久矣。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Liangbi memorialized: "As a general Zhang utterly defeated Song armies; the Song have long hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Liangbi said, "Zhang as a general routed the Song armies. They have hated him for years.

sentences.zh: 將因此陷之死地，未可知也。

translations.literal: They may use this to trap him to his death — that cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: They may have set this trap to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 今若殺璋，或者墮其計中耳。」

translations.literal: If we kill Zhang now, we may fall into their scheme."
translations.idiomatic: If we execute Zhang now, we may be playing into their hands."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，乃杖璋百五十，除名，副使客省使高翊杖百，沒入其所受禮物。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right; Zhang was given one hundred fifty strokes of the staff and dismissed from office; deputy envoy Gaoyi of the Guest Bureau was given one hundred strokes, and the gifts he had received were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. Zhang received one hundred fifty strokes of the staff and was dismissed; deputy envoy Gaoyi of the Guest Bureau received one hundred strokes, and all gifts were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，上念璋有征伐功，起為景州刺史，遷武定軍節度使，授山東西路蒲底山拏兀魯河謀克，改臨洮尹。

translations.literal: More than a year later, remembering Zhang's merit in campaigns, the emperor recalled him as prefect of Jingzhou, transferred him to military commissioner of Wuding Army, granted him meng'an of Pudishan Na'wuluhe on the Shandong West Route, and changed him to grand prefect of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, remembering his campaigns, the emperor recalled him as prefect of Jingzhou, then military commissioner of Wuding Army, granted him the Pudishan Na'wuluhe meng'an on the Shandong West Route, and made him grand prefect of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 19.

sentences.zh: 鄆王昂，本名吾都補，世祖最幼子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yun Ang, original name Wudubu, was Shizu's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yun Ang, born Wudubu, was Shizu's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 常從太祖征伐。

translations.literal: He often followed Taizu on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He often campaigned at Taizu's side.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，昂與稍喝以兵四千監護諸部降人，處之嶺東，就以兵守臨潢府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, Ang and Shaohe with four thousand troops supervised surrendered people of various clans, settled them east of the mountains, and with their troops guarded Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year 6, Ang and Shaohe took four thousand men to supervise surrendered clansmen, resettled them east of the mountains, and garrisoned Linhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昂不能撫禦，降人苦之，多叛亡者。

translations.literal: Ang could not comfort and control them; the surrendered people suffered under him, and many fled in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ang could not govern them well. The surrendered people suffered, and many rebelled and fled.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，使出里底戒諭昂。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he sent Shulidi to admonish Ang.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu heard of it, he sent Shulidi to warn Ang.

sentences.zh: 已過上京，諸部皆叛去，惟章湣宮、小室韋二部達內地。

translations.literal: Before reaching Shangjing, all the clans rebelled and left; only the Zhangmin Palace and Lesser Shiwei two clans reached the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shulidi reached Shangjing, every clan had rebelled and fled. Only the Zhangmin Palace and Lesser Shiwei clans made it into the interior.

sentences.zh: 詔諳版勃極烈吳乞買曰：「比遣昂徙諸部，多致怨叛，稍喝駐兵不與討襲，致使降人複歸遼主，違命失眾，當置重法。

translations.literal: An edict to Anban Bolie Wuqimai said: "Recently in sending Ang to relocate the clans, he caused much resentment and rebellion; Shaohe held his troops and did not join in pursuit, causing surrendered people to return to the Liao ruler — disobeying orders and losing the people. Heavy punishment is due.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Anban Bolie Wuqimai read: "Ang's relocation of the clans provoked widespread rebellion. Shaohe held his troops back and would not pursue, letting the surrendered people return to the Liao ruler. They disobeyed orders and lost the people. They deserve severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 若有所疑，則禁錮之，俟師還定議。」

translations.literal: If there is doubt, imprison them and wait until the army returns to decide."
translations.idiomatic: If there is doubt, imprison them until the army returns and decide then."

sentences.zh: 是時，太宗居守，辭不失副之，辭不失勸太宗因國慶可薄其罰，於是杖昂七十，拘之泰州，而殺稍喝。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong was left in charge; Xishibu assisted him. Xishibu urged Taizong that because of the national celebration the penalty could be lightened; Ang was given seventy strokes and confined at Taizhou, while Shaohe was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was regent at the time, with Xishibu as his deputy. Xishibu urged that the national celebration warranted leniency. Ang received seventy strokes and was confined at Taizhou; Shaohe was executed.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，權元帥左都監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui he was acting Left Overseer of the Marshal's Command.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year 6 he served as acting Left Overseer of the Marshal's Command.

sentences.zh: 十五年，為西京留守。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he became garrison commander of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he became garrison commander of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，為平章政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan he became Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan year 3 he became Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 皇統元年，封漆水郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangtong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qishui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangtong he was made Prince of Qishui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二年，制詔昂暑銜帶「皇叔祖」字，封鄆王。

translations.literal: In the second year an edict was issued that Ang's title on documents should bear the words "Imperial Uncle-Grandfather," and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 an edict required his documents to bear the title Imperial Uncle-Grandfather, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 子 鄭家

translations.literal: Son: Zhengjia
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengjia

sentences.zh: 子鄭家、鶴壽。

translations.literal: Sons Zhengjia and Heshou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhengjia and Heshou.

sentences.zh: 鶴壽累官耶魯瓦群牧使，死於契丹撒八之難，語在《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: Heshou rose through offices to commissioner of the Yeluwa herd; he died in the Khitan Saba rebellion — told in the "Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Heshou rose to commissioner of the Yeluwa herd and died in the Khitan Saba rebellion — an account given in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 鄭家，皇統初，以宗室子授定遠大將軍，除磁州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhengjia: at the beginning of Huangtong, as a member of the imperial clan he was granted General Who Pacifies the Distance and appointed prefect of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Huangtong, Zhengjia was made General Who Pacifies the Distance as a clansman and appointed prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 天德間，為右諫議大夫，累遷會甯尹、安化軍節度使，改益都尹。

translations.literal: During Tiande he was Right Remonstrance Counselor, successively promoted to grand prefect of Huining, military commissioner of Anhua Army, and changed to grand prefect of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiande he was Right Remonstrance Counselor, then grand prefect of Huining, military commissioner of Anhua Army, and finally grand prefect of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，為浙東道副統制，與工部尚書蘇保衡以舟師自海道趨臨安，至松林島阻風，泊島間。

translations.literal: When Hailing campaigned against Song, he was deputy commander of the Zhedong Route; with Minister of Works Su Baoheng he led a fleet by sea toward Lin'an, reached Songlin Island, was blocked by wind, and anchored among the islands.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing attacked Song, Zhengjia was deputy commander of the Zhedong Route. He and Minister of Works Su Baoheng led a fleet by sea toward Lin'an, were becalmed at Songlin Island, and anchored among the islets.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，舟人望見敵舟，請為備。

translations.literal: At dawn the sailors sighted enemy ships and asked to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the sailors sighted enemy ships and asked to prepare for battle.

sentences.zh: 鄭家問：「去此幾何？」

translations.literal: Zhengjia asked: "How far from here are they?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhengjia asked, "How far away are they?"

sentences.zh: 舟人曰：「以水路測之，且三百里。

translations.literal: The sailors said: "By water route it is roughly three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The sailors said, "By sea it is roughly three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 風迅，行即至矣。」

translations.literal: The wind is swift — if they sail they will arrive at once."
translations.idiomatic: With this wind they will be upon us at once."

sentences.zh: 鄭家不曉海路舟楫，不之信。

translations.literal: Zhengjia did not understand sea routes and shipping and did not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengjia knew nothing of sea warfare and did not believe them.

sentences.zh: 有頃，敵果至，見我軍無備，即以火砲擲之。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy indeed arrived; seeing our army unprepared, they at once hurled fire projectiles.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the enemy arrived, found the fleet unprepared, and opened fire with incendiary projectiles.

sentences.zh: 鄭家顧見左右舟中皆火發，度不得脫，赴水死，時年四十一。

translations.literal: Zhengjia looked back and saw fires breaking out in the ships on either side; judging that he could not escape, he threw himself into the water and died, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengjia saw the ships on either side burst into flame, knew he could not escape, threw himself into the sea, and drowned. He was forty-one.
